chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said:

I asked him about the one praying, and he said: 'When a man from the Muslims sends you greetings (salam) while you are in prayer, respond to him inwardly between yourself and your soul, and do not raise your voice.'

key_terms.فِيمَا بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَ نَفْسِكَ: Inwardly / Between oneself and one's soul
key_terms.وَلَا تَرْفَعْ صَوْتَكَ: And do not raise your voice

ai.seo_question: How should a Muslim respond to a greeting while praying?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the etiquette of responding to greetings during prayer, establishing that a silent, inward acknowledgment suffices to maintain the sanctity and concentration (khushu) of the worshipper. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on preserving the continuity of prayer while acknowledging social bonds, distinguishing this silent response from the louder recitation required for the greeting of Allah (Salam al-Kubra) or when addressing multiple people. This hadith is foundational in the chapter on the manner of prayer, illustrating the balance between ritual precision and social interaction within the Islamic tradition.
